subject: Bridge request: temporary onshore processing & subprocessor registry
messages:
From: Jake Miller <jake.miller@finovo.com>
To: connor_obrien@redwood.ai
Cc: Aisha Khan <aisha.khan@finovo.com>
Date: Tue, 01 Jun 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Subprocessor registry + temporary onshore processing request

Hi Connor,

Thanks for taking our call this morning. As we scope the pilot for ingesting Finovo customer telemetry into Redwood, our security team needs a current subprocessor registry and a short-term plan to keep pilot data within the US for the first 30 days.

Specific asks:
- Full subprocessor list (names, function, country of processing)
- Confirmation of where KMS/HSM keys are hosted for the pilot (region)
- Any SOC 2 evidence or on-demand attestations you can share
- Whether Redwood can provide an onshore bridge (US-only processing) for the first 30 days while we complete our internal export reviews

We attached the fields we need to populate our questionnaire (spreadsheet). Can you let me know the expected lead time for the roster and whether an onshore exception is possible?

Also copying Aisha from procurement to track contract redlines.

Best,
Jake
Jake Miller
Head of Platform Security
Finovo Analytics

Attachments: finovo_questionnaire_template.xlsx (spreadsheet)

From: connor_obrien@redwood.ai <connor_obrien@redwood.ai>
To: Jake Miller <jake.miller@finovo.com>
Cc: kimberly_park@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 01 Jun 2026 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Subprocessor registry + temporary onshore processing request

Hi Jake — thanks for the clear list.

Quick answers up front: yes, we can provide a current subprocessor roster and SOC 2 artifacts; and we have an established "temporary onshore bridge" procedure used for pilots (technical and contractual controls).

What I can do today:
- Attached a CSV export of the current subprocessor roster with function and country columns (see requested_subprocessor_roster.csv).
- Attached a short runbook describing the onshore bridge steps and controls (onshore-bridge-runbook.docx).

A few clarifying items BEFORE we stand up the bridge:
1) Pilot scope & retention: please confirm the datasets that will flow and the retention window for the pilot (we typically limit to 30 days for pilots).
2) KMS: our production KMS is multi-region; for the bridge we can ensure keys are provisioned in a US-restricted HSM and provide an attestation.
3) Contract: legal will need a short amendment (30-day residency addendum + acceptance of controls). Kimberly, can you propose language and confirm any escalations for export controls?

Operational timeline suggestion: once we have the dataset definition and signed addendum, we can provision the US-only routing and KMS keys within 48–72 hours.

Let me know if you prefer a quick sync call before signing.

Thanks —
Connor O'Brien
Account Executive, Strategic Sales
Redwood Inference
Phone: (415) 555-0192

Attachments: requested_subprocessor_roster.csv (CSV), onshore-bridge-runbook.docx (Word)

Date: Wed, 02 Jun 2026 10:15:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Subprocessor registry + temporary onshore processing request

Hi all,

Thanks for the background, Connor. I reviewed the roster and runbook. We can support a 30-day US-only processing bridge for a pilot under the following conditions (summary):

- Contract: Finovo signs a narrow DPA addendum that limits scope to the pilot dataset, duration (30 days), and lists the specific subprocessors in scope during the bridge.
- Controls: Redwood will provide a KMS/HSM location attestation and a one-time snapshot of SOC 2 controls relevant to the subprocessors in-scope.
- Audit rights: Finovo gets a limited right to request attestation evidence within the pilot window (for example, a signed statement and redacted reports).
- Export controls: If the data contains export-restricted elements, we need completion of Finovo's export questionnaire prior to activation.

I'll push a short addendum template and a marked-up DPA redline (see redlines_finovo_dpa_v1.pdf). Marissa — FYI on onboarding steps and any billing/pricing for the bridge.

Connor — once Finovo confirms dataset boundaries and signs the addendum, legal can sign off, and ops will proceed with provisioning.

—Kimberly
Kimberly Park
Senior Counsel, Privacy & Security
Redwood Inference

Attachments: redlines_finovo_dpa_v1.pdf (PDF)
